recommended_use: Creating environments or products suited to specific needs (relaxation, concentration, alertness); enhancing functionality of luminaires; improving physiological aspects and appeal of areas; enabling tailored design.
limitations: Most effects of light and colour have been studied in controlled laboratory conditions under artificial light, which may limit their general applicability to real-world scenarios.
Technical challenges and inherent variability pose a significant obstacle for studies utilising natural daylight.
Lack sufficient data to substantiate the claim conclusively for intuitive preference for daylight over artificial light.
The complex nature of the human perception process.
Inherent subjectivity of colour perception and its emotional effects, rooted in cultural, personal and psychological factors.
Lack of Proper Color Control: Many studies do not adequately control colour properties, often only addressing them at device level rather than the spectral level.

Neglect of Environmental Factors: Color perception is influenced by various environmental factors such as viewing distance, lighting conditions, and the presence of other colours, often ignored in psychological research.
Underpowered Samples: Many studies in this area suffer from small sample sizes, which can lead to overestimated effect sizes and premature conclusions.
Contamination of the survey colour, often not “administered” correctly.
Designing a test to assess emotional responses in subjects is a highly complex endeavour.

Numerous factors influence test outcomes: geometry of the room, choice of furnishings/objects, presence/absence of other persons, psycho-physical state of subjects (fatigue, boredom, stress, excitement), sleep duration, age, gender, profession.
It is infrequent to be in environments illuminated monochromatically, making single-colour studies less ecologically valid.
Several variables impact the time required to conduct the test on each subject, making it challenging to address all issues.
The number of variables to consider when evaluating human emotions is very high.
